text:
Sasha: quick check — planning to enable flag `enable_new_routing_v2` tomorrow for a small canary. proposed slices: web=10%, mobile_app=5%. are those slices guaranteed disjoint? wondering about logged-in mobile web users who might qualify for both.

Mateo: they come from different audience definitions. web uses cookie-based bucketing, mobile_app uses device id. overlap possible if we have same user_id on both.

Olivia: +1 on overlap. for experiments we usually dedupe by user_id across channels, but rollout flags in prod runtime sometimes don't. which system will own dedup?

Sasha: ExperimentRunner will run the A/B, but the flag evaluation is in the routing runtime. need to decide where to enforce dedupe. small prod-level change is riskier.

Mateo: recommendation: enforce dedupe at ExperimentRunner (pre-routing) for the A/B cohort only. keep flag evaluation consistent for rollouts (so non-experiment traffic sees the flag as usual).

Lucas: sounds reasonable. any guardrails we should add before flipping to 10%? thinking latency and error-rate checks plus success-metric sanity.

Anya: propose stop criteria:
- 95th pct latency increase > 10% relative to baseline for 5m
- error rate (5xx) increase > 0.5 percentage points for 5m
- absolute CTR uplift < 0.2% (so we can kill if harming conversion)

Sasha: adding that. also need to ensure sample independence for A/B stats — if overlap persists stats are invalid. can we log overlap_count as metric?

Mateo: yes. ExperimentRunner can emit `experiment.overlap_count` and `experiment.dedup_applied=true/false`. we'll also emit cohort_id for each eval.

Sasha: sample of config I plan to push to experiment-runner (pseudo):

```json
{
  "experiment_id": "exp_enable_routing_v2_2027_01",
  "cohorts": {
    "control": 0.85,
    "treatment_web": 0.10,
    "treatment_mobile": 0.05
  },
  "dedupe_key_priority": ["user_id", "device_id"],
  "stop_criteria": {
    "latency_95_pct_increase_pct": 10,
    "error_rate_increase_pp": 0.5,
    "min_observations": 1000
  }
}
```

Olivia: looks good. one ask: can we make mobile treatment explicitly exclude users already in web treatment to avoid contamination?

Mateo: yes, we can implement exclusion rule: assign web cohort first, then exclude those IDs when assigning mobile cohort. order matters.

Sasha: good. add step in rollout playbook:
1) dry-run in staging with dedupe on
2) deploy ExperimentRunner config with `dedupe=true` and log overlap metrics to /observability/experiments
3) open canary at 1% for 30m, check stop criteria
4) expand to 5% mobile / 10% web if stable

Anya: can someone own the observability dashboard? I can wire alerts but need the panel config.

Lucas: I can create the panels — will include: traffic by cohort, overlap_count, 95th latency by cohort, 5xx rate by cohort, key business metric. tagging with `exp_enable_routing_v2_2027_01`.

DeployBot: deployment scheduled: `routing-service` config push queued for 2027-01-30 09:15 UTC.

ExperimentRunner: config validated. dedupe rule syntax OK. expected sample rate match: 1000 reqs/min across all cohorts.

Sasha: ok assigning owners:
- ExperimentRunner config + canary runs: @Mateo
- Dashboard + alerts: @Lucas
- Rollout playbook + postmortem: @Anya
- Runtime flag review (runtime semver/compat): @Olivia

Mateo: I'll kick off the dry-run later today and post a short log here once done.

Olivia: quick note — make sure the runtime flag fallback path is documented in playbook in case we need immediate kill switch.

Sasha: noted. thanks everyone. ping here with dry-run result or if you spot any config mismatch. :thumbsup:

Mateo: dry-run complete — no overlaps in staging after dedupe enabled, logs: `overlap_count=0` for 30m. pushing canary later today.

Lucas: dashboard created and alert set: `exp_enable_routing_v2_2027_01_overlap>10` -> page on-call.

Anya: playbook PR up at https://git.redwood/infrastructure/playbooks/pull/312 — includes kill switch steps and rollback checklist.

Sasha: perfect. moving to canary phase in 1h. will update thread with first 30m snapshot.

(End of thread)
